hypotheses.name: Signed paired-throw basement-gravity concordance under low-relief alluvial cover
layers: competition det_elev (Band 12, USGS DOI 10.5066/P9MQRCBY) and det_elev_slope (Band 19)
hypotheses.signature: Test antisymmetric flank profiles across +/-400 m strike-oriented corridors: a positive hanging-wall step in depth_to_base_surf (Band 15) and a negative step in iso_grav_anom (Band 13) must share the same downthrown polarity along >=900 m strike continuity, weighted higher where det_elev (Band 12) and det_elev_slope (Band 19) scarp relief is muted by Holocene basin fill, and compared against a polarity-scrambled control at identical 300 m submodular emission budget.
hypotheses.why_unmapped: Hypothesis: burial by alluvial or playa sediments may obscure surface scarps while leaving basement-depth and gravity steps. Test enrichment on withheld whole segments before claiming preferential recovery of catalogue-missing faults. These two layers may share gravity-inversion ancestry and must not be treated as independent evidence without provenance checks.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: All executed GEMSDOE86 lanes (GMC, RMRB, WVB, GFCO, KSLB, CTHB) rely on unsigned gradient magnitudes, tilt zero-crossings, or Blakely curvature ridges and discard cross-flank dip-slip polarity concordance; PR #60 mentioned signed paired-throw in prose without ever loading training_features.tif or implementing it (IR-86-SPT-02).
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Unfaulted pre-Tertiary erosional paleovalley margins or buried caldera moat walls infilled by low-density tuffaceous basin sediments; gravity-basement inversion artifacts.
hypotheses.expected_dti_gain: First qualitative testing priority among local-feature candidates, not measured or projected DTI improvement. Historical owner-reported scores cannot establish which geological regime caused a difference.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: Low-medium: oriented +/-400 m antisymmetric flank filters, polarity-scrambled control, and existing 300 m submodular decoder.
hypotheses.data_readiness: NOT_READY: raw competition layers have pinned mirrors, but execution remains blocked by protocol_preflight.require_feasible() under the literal 17GEMSDOE dense-witness rule.

hypotheses.name: Cross-corridor GeoDAWN magnetic marker-horizon phase-correlation offset
layers: competition tc (Band 6; physical meaning not independently verified here, excluded pending metadata verification) and tmi_hg (Band 3)
mirrored external geodawn_rad_u8.tif K/Th/U radiometrics (GeoDAWN DOI 10.5066/P93LGLVQ)
hypotheses.signature: Hypothesis: phase-correlate transverse rtp (Band 2) magnetic markers on opposite flanks of label-free candidate corridors. Require consistent lateral translation across adjacent strike windows and compare with zero-shift and phase-scrambled controls. Do not use tc until authoritative band semantics are verified. Estimate survey-seam directions from acquisition metadata before defining a seam veto, rather than assuming fixed compass azimuths.
hypotheses.why_unmapped: Accommodation-zone transfer faults and oblique Walker Lane / Humboldt relay structures cut buried Tertiary volcanic sheets across basin floors without building prominent range-front topographic scarps, leaving coherent lateral marker offsets where surface mapping is blank.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: GFCO compares TMI (Band 14) with upward-continued TMI; GMC computes cross-gradients between iso_grav_anom (Band 13) and rtp (Band 2); WVB and CTHB use local-wavenumber, tilt-phase, and hydrothermal couplings. None estimate two-sided flank-to-flank lateral phase translation of transverse magnetic markers.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Unfaulted intrusive contacts, primary Miocene lava-flow lobe terminations, GeoDAWN E-W (200/400 m) flight-line and N-S (2000/4000 m) tie-line leveling seams, and remanent magnetization reversals.
hypotheses.expected_dti_gain: Second qualitative priority: physically orthogonal strike-slip / transfer-zone detector using local and mirrored GeoDAWN bands without new external downloads. No score projection.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: Medium-high: multi-azimuth split-window FFT phase correlation, E-W/N-S survey-seam suppression, and buffered LOQO validation (~65 min CPU).
hypotheses.data_readiness: NOT_READY: blocked prior to feature construction by protocol_preflight.require_feasible() under the pinned dense-witness overlap stop.

hypotheses.name: Hydrothermal magnetite-destruction trough & pairwise paleo-vent/sinter strike-alignment corridor
layers: competition rtp (Band 2), tmi_vg (Band 9), cond_surf (Band 17), geod_dilaterate (Band 8), and geod_shearrate (Band 7)
mirrored DOE GDR 1391 paleo_geothermal_regional.zip (726 sinter/tufa deposits, sha256 faffcf69...) and 2m_temperature_probe_INGENIOUS_regional_data.zip (3,800 probes, sha256 1301f70d...)
mirrored DOE GDR 1391 gdr_volcanic_vents_in_footprint.csv and gdr_wellspring_in_footprint.csv (excluding dist_known_fault_px) + geodawn_extensions_u8.tif K/Th & U/Th
hypotheses.signature: Hypothesis: extract strike-continuous rtp (Band 2) minima with positive cross-strike second derivative of rtp (equivalently negative second derivative of -rtp) and flanking shoulders. Compare magnetic response, thermal-point alignments and conductance/dilatancy with phase-scrambled and point-location controls. A magnetic trough alone is not diagnostic of magnetite destruction; remanence, source geometry, lithology and acquisition artifacts can produce it. Do not assume tmi_vg extrema have the same polarity as rtp minima.
hypotheses.why_unmapped: Hypothesis: hydrothermal alteration along buried conduits may change magnetic susceptibility without a mapped surface scarp. The fraction of blind systems and alteration mineralogy are not established by this local review, and neither implies that a predicted corridor is a fault or a vent.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: H86D-CTHB extracted only positive magnetic Hessian ridges (mag_ridge_s15) and radially isotropic point halos around sinter/volcanic vents (paleo_sinter_vent, volcanic_vent_halo); no lane in GEMSDOE86 extracts negative flanking-shoulder magnetite-destruction troughs or pairwise co-linear vent-to-vent geodesic corridors.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Non-tectonic reversed-polarity volcanic flows, felsic ash-flow tuffs with primary low magnetic susceptibility, or E-W/N-S GeoDAWN tie-line troughs.
hypotheses.expected_dti_gain: Third qualitative testing priority; no measured or projected DTI gain. The competition prediction target is missing fault traces, not direct vent classification. Mirrored point layers require provenance and catalogue-leakage checks before use.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: Medium: signed valley-curvature filter on rtp/tmi_vg, pairwise vent-alignment Radon/geodesic corridor builder, and buffered whole-component LOQO (~45 min CPU).
hypotheses.data_readiness: NOT_READY: all competition and GDR 1391 sinter/2m-probe/vent inputs are SHA-pinned on GitHub mirrors (research/h86d_extended_manifest.json), but execution remains blocked by protocol_preflight.require_feasible() under the literal 17GEMSDOE dense-witness rule.

hypotheses.name: Multi-depth 3D MT conductance contrast x conductive heat-flow & transtensional dilatancy bridge
layers: external USGS Great Basin 3D MT electrical conductance slices (5 depth ranges 2-200 km, DOI 10.5066/P9TWT2LU)
external USGS Great Basin conductive heat-flow grids (DOI 10.5066/P9BZPVUC)
competition cond_surf (Band 17), geod_dilaterate (Band 8), geod_shearrate (Band 7), and tc (Band 6)
hypotheses.signature: Hypothesis: compare conductance gradients across verified depth intervals, heat-flow context and geodetic dilatancy. First verify official release depth bins and resolution; do not assume a shallow interval exists or that coarse regional MT grids resolve 100 m fault corridors. Exclude tc until its physical meaning is independently verified.
hypotheses.why_unmapped: Blind hydrothermal fault conduits in the Humboldt structural zone and northern Walker Lane frequently lack Holocene surface scarps and modern catalog seismicity, yet deep saline upflow + smectite-illite clay alteration produce multi-kilometer MT conductance steps inside actively dilating crust.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: Training_features.tif provides only single-surface cond_surf (Band 17) plus geodetic bands (Bands 4, 7, 8), which conflate shallow playa brines with deep fault conduits; no GEMSDOE86 lane ingests the 5-depth USGS 3D MT conductance slices (10.5066/P9TWT2LU) or USGS conductive heat-flow release (10.5066/P9BZPVUC).
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Stratiform Paleozoic graphitic/sulfidic marine black shales (e.g., Roberts Mountains thrust allochthon) generating deep non-geothermal crustal conductance.
hypotheses.expected_dti_gain: Fourth qualitative priority: resolves the shallow-playa vs deep-conduit ambiguity of Band 17 cond_surf, gated behind ScienceBase raster mirroring and coarse-to-100 m downscaling verification. No score projection.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: Medium-high: USGS ScienceBase archive pinning, EPSG:32611 reprojection, depth-ratio differencing, leakage-canary check, and buffered holdout testing.
hypotheses.free_official_source_needed: USGS ScienceBase Electrical Conductance Maps of the Great Basin (https://doi.org/10.5066/P9TWT2LU, Peacock & Bedrosian 2022) and Heat Flow Maps of the Great Basin (https://doi.org/10.5066/P9BZPVUC, DeAngelo et al. 2022), public domain.
hypotheses.obtainability: NOT_VERIFIED_THIS_SESSION: the listed USGS DOI releases are prospective official sources. ScienceBase and DOI hosts are outside the sandbox allowlist; official archive bytes, depth intervals, license and spatial coverage have not been independently retrieved here.
hypotheses.data_readiness: NOT_VIABLE_YET: official multi-depth MT and heat-flow bytes, metadata, coverage and license require verification and pinning; protocol preflight also blocks execution.

hypotheses.name: Watershed-crossing 1-m 3DEP LiDAR micro-scarp curvature persistence
layers: official USGS 3DEP bare-earth 1 m DEM tiles (competition 1m_DEM_links.csv)
hypotheses.signature: Measure signed 5-25 m cross-strike profile curvature steps on native 1 m bare-earth LiDAR DEMs that retain strike and downthrown polarity across independently delineated drainage divides, vetoing candidates aligned with steepest-descent channels, constant-elevation pluvial shorelines, or road embankments.
hypotheses.why_unmapped: Low-slip (0.3-1.5 m) late Quaternary piedmont and intrabasin scarps are smoothed below noise in 30-100 m DEM products (det_elev Band 12, det_elev_slope Band 19) and missed in pre-LiDAR airphoto mapping, yet persist cleanly across multiple ephemeral fan catchments at 1 m LiDAR resolution.
hypotheses.difference_from_repo: Zero GEMSDOE86 lanes ingest raw native 1 m 3DEP LiDAR tiles (prior lanes used only pre-quantized 100 m summary bands in lidar_scarp_features_u8.tif without cross-divide polarity persistence).
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Pleistocene Lake Lahontan wave-cut shoreline benches, fluvial terrace risers, and highway/railroad grades.
hypotheses.expected_dti_gain: Fifth qualitative testing priority because native-resolution processing and data acquisition are costly; no measured or projected DTI improvement.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: High: native-resolution terrain processing and drainage-divide conditioning. Not admitted within this session budget until a measured small-area benchmark establishes feasibility; stop at the two-hour limit.
hypotheses.free_official_source_needed: USGS 3DEP 1 m bare-earth DEM GeoTIFFs indexed by the competition's 1m_DEM_links.csv (documented in https://docs.nlr.gov/docs/fy26osti/96647.pdf).
hypotheses.obtainability: NOT_VERIFIED_THIS_SESSION: USGS 3DEP is the prospective official source. Native tiles and the competition coverage manifest are absent; official tile hosts are outside this sandbox allowlist. No claim of current download availability is made.
hypotheses.data_readiness: NOT_VIABLE_YET: native 1 m DEM tiles and coverage manifest are not present in this checkout, and protocol_preflight.require_feasible() blocks model execution.

required_validation_after_blockers_are_r: Assign one method lane; restore and hash-verify the actual shared cached feature stack and a current complete accessible registry.

Resolve both literal saturation witnesses upstream in 60GEMSDOE (the 17GEMSDOE 100%-allowed continuous surface ab0a0a62... AND the 13GEMSDOE 99.87%-covered stride-5 discrete dot lattice b4570b40..., which forces >=82.70% 3-px overlap on any 37,654-dot raster by pigeonhole); never patch vendor/gems57 privately.

Freeze buffered whole-component folds and fixed budgets before touching withheld labels; derive every catalogue feature strictly from fold-visible faults outside the buffer (never mask full existing_faults.tif as PR #60 did).
Run single-feature and combined leakage canaries before trusting any holdout number; max(AUC, 1-AUC) > 0.90 stops the run, and AUC <= 0.52 flags a non-informative feature.

Use the pinned shared evaluate_holdout.py and submission_writer.py unchanged; report pooled HOLDOUT-DTI with evaluator version, withheld-positive pixel count, physical-block 95% CI, and paired delta vs H86D-CTHB and fold-fair R0.
At most 3 experiments or 2 hours per session; negative results are first-class deliverables, and promotion to a DrivenData weekly submission slot remains a separate selector step.
evidence_boundary: All physical signatures, catalogue-missing rationales and benefit rankings below are untested hypotheses, not verified discoveries or expected scores. Official URLs identify prospective sources, not fresh verification of their contents. Owner mirrors do not authenticate organizer data.
